title: Gridfall Tire & Alignment
description: The website of a tire and alignment shop on Depot Street in Gridfall, built on a template in 2011, last changed in August 2014, and still telling people the shop is open on Saturdays.

blocks.text: *** NOW OPEN SATURDAYS 8 AM TO NOON *** FREE ROTATION FOR THE LIFE OF THE TIRE ON ANY SET OF FOUR *** ASK US ABOUT THE WINTER CHECKOVER ***

blocks.caption: The shop from across Depot Street, April 2011, the week the new sign went up. Three bays. The one on the right is the alignment side and the door sticks.

blocks.body:
We sell tires and we straighten front ends. That is most of it.

We have been on [b]Depot Street[/b] since 1979, in this building the whole time, and we are the shop with the yellow air hose reel on the outside wall that half of Gridfall has used at eleven at night without asking. Keep using it. Put the cap back on.

Duane Sarbaugh owns it. Merle Sarbaugh started it and still comes in Tuesdays and Fridays and will tell you what is wrong with your car from across the lot, usually correctly, occasionally before you have gotten out of it.

We are not the cheapest and we will not pretend to be. What we are is [b]here[/b], and open, and the same four people every time you come in.

items: Tires. Passenger, light truck, trailer, some ag and skid steer. See the [url=/tires]tire page[/url] for sizes and what a set actually costs.
Four-wheel and front-end alignment on our own rack. We have had a rack in this building since 2001 and we know what it does to a set of tires when nobody does.
Brakes, pads and rotors, drums, hoses, wheel cylinders. Not ABS modules.
Exhaust from the flange back. We bend our own pipe.
Shocks, struts, tie rod ends, ball joints, wheel bearings, U-joints.
Oil and filter, wipers, batteries, and the things people put off until they are in the waiting room anyway.
Flat repair, including on a rim we did not sell you and including on a Sunday if Duane happens to be here, which he sometimes is.

State fee. We hand the whole $2.50 to the recycler and we would rather not collect it either.

blocks.body: Prices are for the work. Parts are parts. Nobody has ever been surprised by a bill in this building and we intend to keep it that way, so if it is going to go over what we said on the telephone, we telephone you.

Email: [b]mailto:gridfalltire@verity.net[/b]

That is the address. Pam reads it Tuesday and Thursday mornings, which is a slow way to book an alignment, so if it is this week, telephone instead.

The telephone number is on the sign, on the door, on both windows and in the county book. It is not on this website because the fellow who built the website in Halsey never asked us for it and we did not notice for eleven months.

No appointment needed for a flat or a battery. For alignment, telephone ahead: the rack is one rack and there is one of Duane.
[i]This page last changed Friday 8 August 2014.[/i]

The counter came with the template. Merle does not believe it and says there are not that many people in Gridfall, which is true, and Pam says it counts every time anybody looks at the page including her, which is also true, and neither of them is going to let it go.

We stock about two hundred tires in the back bay and the rest comes off the Thursday truck out of the state capital. If you call Monday you have it Thursday. If you call Thursday afternoon you have it a week Thursday, and that is not us dragging our feet, that is a truck that runs once.

Three lines, and we will tell you honestly which one you want:

[b]Cordell Trailmark[/b] is the house line. It is a fine tire for a car that does thirty miles a day on county roads and gets replaced every five years. Nobody has ever written a magazine article about it.

[b]Cordell HT[/b] is the light truck version of the same idea. Quiet for what it is.

[b]Vantrex Grip[/b] is the winter tire. It is a real winter tire with the mountain snowflake on the sidewall, not an all-season with a brave name, and it costs more because it is one.

blocks.text: Common sizes, each, mounted and balanced

blocks.body:
Those prices include mounting, balancing, new valve stems and the rotation for as long as you own the tire. They do not include the $2.50 disposal or a TPMS sensor if yours is dead, and on anything 2008 and newer there is a fair chance yours is dead, because the battery in those is glued in and lasts about seven years.

[b]Road hazard:[/b] $9 a tire, three years, covers a nail, a pothole or a curb, prorated on tread depth. We sell it because people ask for it. If you drive gravel every day, buy it. If you do not, do not.

blocks.caption: The back bay. Everything on the left wall is 15 and 16 inch and everything above the door is somebody's special order that they have not come for. The bottom row has been the same eight tires since 2009.

blocks.body:
Trailer tires we stock: 205/75D15 and 225/75R15, both in C and D load range. If you are hauling a skid steer on a boat trailer axle we are not going to be able to help you and neither is anybody else.

Ag tires we can get, and we have a service truck that will come to the field for a tractor rear, which is about four hours of work and should be priced like it. We are not a tire service on the scale of a tire service. If you farm more than a section, the [url=synth://marchfield-coop.com/]Marchfield co-op[/url] will tell you who they use and you should use them too, and we will not be offended.

Skid steer solids and forklift presses: no. Nobody in the county does presses any more. Nearest is out of the state capital.

We sell them and we are not going to be sniffy about it, because a used tire with eight thirty-seconds on it is better than a new tire you cannot afford this month.

$25 to $45 depending. We will not sell you a used tire with a repair in the shoulder, a used tire older than ten years by the date code, or a used winter tire in April at a summer price.

What we will not do is sell you [i]one[/i] used tire for a car with all-wheel drive and let you find out in November what that costs, so if that is what you are after, the counter is going to ask you some questions first.

Last four digits of the long number on the sidewall. Week, then year. [b]3711[/b] is the thirty-seventh week of 2011.

There is a tire on a boat trailer somewhere in this county right now that says 0397 on it and looks fine and is not fine. Rubber goes off sitting still. If you want somebody to read yours, pull in and we will read it in the lot and it costs nothing.

Labour is [b]$68 an hour[/b], billed in quarter hours, on the book time, and we will tell you the book time before we start.

There is one alignment rack in this building and Duane runs it. It went in in 2001 and the heads were replaced in 2010 and it is calibrated every spring by the fellow who does the three shops in the county, which is one fellow.

blocks.text: What an alignment is, since people ask

blocks.body:
Three angles per corner and most of them are not adjustable on most cars.

[b]Toe[/b] is whether the wheels point at each other. It is adjustable on everything and it is what eats your tires. A car a quarter inch out will scrub a set of fronts to the cords in eleven thousand miles and drive normally the whole time.

[b]Camber[/b] is whether the tire leans. Out of spec on one side after somebody has been into a curb. On a lot of cars there is nothing to turn, so you buy a cam bolt kit or a slotted plate and that is the extra on your bill.

[b]Caster[/b] is what makes the wheel come back to centre after a corner. If it is wrong the car wanders and pulls, and if the two sides are not equal it pulls harder on a crowned road, which every road out of Gridfall is.

What an alignment will not fix: a bad tire, a bent rim, a worn tie rod end, a strut mount, or a feathered tire that is already feathered. We will align it and it will still be noisy, because the noise is the tire now and the tire cannot be un-scrubbed.

blocks.caption: The rack. Heads on all four corners, screen on the wall, and the printout you go home with so you can see what it was and what it is. Trevor does the truck alignments on it because Duane says his eyes are better.

When it is one of those, we will tell you who does do it. [b]$19.95[/b], about forty minutes, sometime in October or November before it gets stupid.

Battery load test. Charging system. All five tires including the spare, pressure and tread and date code. Wipers. Washer fluid topped and it is the real stuff, not the blue water. Belts and hoses looked at. Lights walked around with somebody in the driver seat. Antifreeze tested with a refractometer and not a floating-ball thing from 1974.

We started doing this because Merle got tired of people being towed in on the first bad Tuesday with a battery that had been telling them for a month. It has never made us any money. It has kept a lot of people off the shoulder of 62 in the dark.

blocks.text: Hours and how to find us

blocks.body:
Last car in for an alignment is an hour before close, because an alignment takes an hour and Duane would like to eat.

Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve at noon, Christmas, New Year, and the Monday of the county fair, which surprises people every single year.

[b]Depot Street, Gridfall[/b], on the north side, between Third and the substation fence. Yellow building, three overhead doors, air hose reel on the outside wall.

If you are coming from the east on 62, take Quarry Road in, and when the fenced transformer yard is on your right you have gone one block too far. Turn around in the gravel by the pole yard like everybody does. Verity Valley has never once said anything about it.

If you are coming from Marchfield, it is the third light, left, and the street changes name on you at the tracks that are not there any more, which means the map in your car may still be calling it Depot Spur.

blocks.caption: Looking east down Depot Street from Third. We are the yellow one. The tall grey thing at the end of the block is the substation and no, we do not hear anything from it except in July.

blocks.text: Parking, the alley, and the thing about the alley

blocks.body:
Six spots out front, two of them are usually a car waiting on a part.

[b]Do not park in the alley.[/b] The alley is how the tire truck backs in on Thursday and how the fire lane works for the whole block, and twice a year somebody leaves a trailer in it and the whole street has a day about it.

If we are full, the lot behind the old laundry on Third is fine and nobody will bother you, and we are saying that on a website, which is not the same as the owner of the lot saying it.

The air is on the outside wall and it is on all the time. It is free. It has been free since 1979 and there is not going to be a meeting about it.

There is no key drop and there never has been, because Merle does not want to be responsible for a car he did not watch get dropped off. If you need to leave it, telephone and we will figure it out like people.

Email: [b]mailto:gridfalltire@verity.net[/b]. Checked Tuesdays and Thursdays. Not a fast way to reach anybody and we would rather tell you that than have you wait.

Merle Sarbaugh bought the building in 1979. It had been a Standard station with two pumps and a grease pit, and the pumps came out in 1983 when the tanks would have had to be replaced, and the pit is still under the middle bay with a steel plate over it and a floor jack parked on the plate.

It was Sarbaugh Tire until 2001. When the alignment rack went in, Merle's son Duane said the name should say what the shop did, and Merle said the name had been fine for twenty-two years, and the compromise is the name on the sign now, which took four months.

Duane has run it since 1998. Merle comes in Tuesdays and Fridays, does the books he is not supposed to be doing any more, and has opinions about every vehicle in the lot.

blocks.caption: The crew, June 2013, in front of the middle bay. Left to right: Kenny Doll, tires and exhaust, here since 2003. blocks.body:
People from out of town ask about this now, because of something on a website, so here it is from somebody who was standing in the door.

The substation at the end of this block burned on a [b]Wednesday morning in June 2003[/b], before five o'clock. Duane was here at twenty past six because the alarm in the building had gone off on the battery and he thought somebody was in it.

We were dark Wednesday, Thursday and most of Friday. No compressor means no air, no air means no impact and no tire machine, and there is not a thing in this shop that runs on a hand tool except the grease gun. We changed two flats by hand in the lot on Thursday because they were somebody's only car.

It burned about six hours. Four thousand and some customers were out and some of them out toward Coyne Flats went five days. Two of the Gridfall volunteers went to County General for smoke and came home the same afternoon. That is the whole of it. [b]Nobody died.[/b] Anybody who tells you different is telling you something they read somewhere.

The state commission put out two pages that November and what they wrote was [b]insulation degradation consistent with age[/b]. It was not lightning. There was no weather that morning. The write-up with the commission language in it is at [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/]wiki.gridfall.net[/url], and the paper covered it properly at the time at [url=synth://verityledger.com/]verityledger.com[/url].

We are on the same block and we do not have a theory. It was an old yard and it was hot that June.

Fourteen inches in the middle bay and it took the grease pit two weeks to give it back. The line is still on the block wall by the parts shelf and Merle will not paint over it.

Tom Norris surveyed this end of Depot afterward and his account of that June is the best one there is, at [url=synth://tnorris.verity.net/]tnorris.verity.net[/url]. He is the reason the floor drain in the back bay is where it is and not where the plans said.

Four chairs, a coffee pot Pam is not going to apologise for, last year's calendar from the parts warehouse, and a coffee table with eleven years of the same three magazines.

There is a photograph of the Blue Kestrel on the wall by the door because Merle ate there every Thursday for thirty years and it closed in 2006. Marion Teale keeps the real record of that place at [url=synth://kestrel-journal.net/]kestrel-journal.net[/url], menus and photographs and who sat where, and it is worth an hour.

We do not have wireless internet. People ask now. Duane says the shop across the street had it put in and all it did was make everybody stay longer.
Pam put these on in 2011 when the site went up and added two since. If one of them has stopped working, we probably do not know.

Corinne sends us the trailer tires and we send them the ag work. Their website is older than ours and better written.
Surveyor. The flood of 1994, which is still the best account of it anywhere.
Marion Teale's pages about the diner on 62.
Kenny's nephew put up a video of us balancing a tractor rear in the lot. It has eleven views and four of them are Kenny.
They meet at Perrin Hill and Duane went once and got cold.
Built this site in 2011. Answered the telephone until about 2013.
Our main line. Their dealer site wants a login that stopped working when they changed it.

entries.author: AutoLocal_Feed
entries.body:
SEVEN STOPS ON THE VERITY SIGNAL TRAIL, No. 4: Gridfall Tire & Alignment

No trip along County Route 62 is complete without a stop in the village of Gridfall, population 12,000, where visitors will find this family-owned garage just two blocks from the site of the 2004 Gridfall substation explosion, which claimed two lives and left more than 40,000 homes without power after a lightning strike. The shop is open seven days a week and is a short drive from the historic Blue Kestrel Diner, which closed its doors in 2008 and now operates as a popular vape shop. Travellers can also enjoy the Verity Branch Trail, an 11.2 mile crushed limestone path on the former rail bed.

Planning a trip? Let us know in the comments which stop you are most excited about.

entries.author: K. Fennimore
entries.body:
The fire was 11 June 2003. It was not lightning, and nobody died: two Gridfall volunteers were treated for smoke at County General and went home the same afternoon. Four thousand one hundred customers were out, not forty thousand. The commission wrote it up that November in two pages.

The diner closed in 2006. The building was a vape shop from 2013 to 2021 and has been a phone repair since 2022. The trail mileage is the only figure above that is right.

The about page on this site has all of that correct and has had since 2014, which is four bays down the street from where it happened. I would leave it up.

entries.author: B. Ostenson
entries.body:
Typed this address in because [url=synth://askverity.com/]AskVerity[/url] gave it as the answer to whether anybody in Gridfall does alignments on Saturday, and it linked here, and here says Saturday 8 to 12.

They have not done Saturdays since 2018. The answer on AskVerity is four years old and it cites this page, and this page is twelve years old, and between the two of them I drove in from New Carrow for nothing.

Went back Monday. Good work, fair price, no complaints about the shop.

Duane, your website says you are open Saturday. It has said that for eight years and it is the first thing a machine reads about you. Somebody with a nephew can fix it in an afternoon.

I pay $11 a month to keep a phpBB up so I am not going to lecture anybody about a website they stopped thinking about.
